# Private MCP Registry

## Caption

Public discovery is not the same thing as private governance. Internal MCP servers need owners, status, review, and approved install paths. Intertool gives teams a private registry for MCP servers and the rest of their agent capability stack.

#MCP #ModelContextProtocol #DeveloperTools #DevEx #AIGovernance #AIInfrastructure #Intertool

## Alt Text

1. Internal MCP servers need a private registry. Your most useful servers are often the ones that should never be public.
2. List servers with owners, status, and scope. Give developers discovery without turning private configs into tribal knowledge.
3. Approve the server before it reaches the team. MCP access becomes a workflow, not a copied JSON blob.
4. One install path across agent surfaces. Claude, Codex, Cursor, Copilot, and custom clients can point to the same source.
5. Keep private tools out of public discovery. Use org-scoped access, private storage, and audit history.
6. Make MCP discoverable inside your company. Intertool is the private catalog for your agent infrastructure.
